Applied.Outcome: Resolved with no reply: the recommendation went in. session.js hands every token to the app through SetToken; a request with no Authorization gets the latest; with no token the proxy answers 401 "sign in".

Replies.Text:
How the proxy gets the person's token. The page signs in through Clerk and asks clerk.session.getToken() before each call; the token lives about a minute and Clerk refreshes it. The proxy, in the main process, has no Clerk session of its own. Two ways: (a) the page hands the token to the app (a SetToken on the bridge) at load and at each refresh, and the proxy puts it on a request that carries none; (b) the main process signs in on its own, with Clerk's backend keys, and keeps a token of its own, which means a second sign-in and the secret keys in the app.

Recommendation: (a), SetToken from the page, as the plan says: session.js calls it with every token it gets, the main process keeps the latest and its expiry, and a request to /api with no Authorization gets it; with no token yet (nobody signed in) the proxy answers 401 "sign in", as a Server would. Resolve with no reply to take it.
